subject.title: fix: sleep tool — session-targeted wake, correct sandbox policy, doc fixes

question: Should OpenClaw accept a first-class core `sleep` tool now, and should the permanent implementation be an agent-scoped cron wrapper or a dedicated Gateway resume primitive?
rationale: The PR adds a new model-facing core scheduling capability that crosses session-state, cron authorization, sandbox/tool-policy, and user-interruption semantics; automation can identify the concrete defects but cannot choose the product/API contract.

options.title: Sponsor corrected core sleep
options.body: Accept the feature direction but require the supported scoped scheduling path, catalog/display registration, schema alignment, same-session proof, and explicit interruption/restart semantics before merge.

options.title: Keep cron as the scheduling surface
options.body: Reject a separate core sleep tool for now and keep delayed work on existing cron, process, and subagent yield surfaces.

options.title: Define an extension seam first
options.body: Pause this PR until maintainers decide whether optional wait/sleep behavior should live outside the default core tool surface.

recommendation.title: Sponsor corrected core sleep
recommendation.body: Accept the feature direction but require the supported scoped scheduling path, catalog/display registration, schema alignment, same-session proof, and explicit interruption/restart semantics before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent history shows the strongest overlap across agent tools, cron session targeting, catalog metadata, and the sibling yield primitive.
